title: Edge GPU onboarding: zero-trust IaC patterns and CI/CD runbook
author: Alex Chen
body:
Summary

This document describes a standardized, zero-trust IaC pattern and associated CI/CD runbook for onboarding new edge GPU pools (on-prem or cloud-edge sites). It combines Terraform modules, network guardrails, CI jobs, preflight validation, and a short operational runbook for day-0/day-1 capacity and safety checks. The goal is to make onboarding reproducible, secure, and measurable with minimal ad-hoc manual steps.

Scope

- Target environments: edge-colocated racks, partner co-lo, AWS Outposts, GCP Anthos (edge).
- Components covered: GPU node provisioning, VPC & routing, egress fencing, identity & certs, warm-pool registration, and CI/CD promotion paths.
- Not covered: tenant application-level SLO tuning, model serving configuration.

Owner and contacts

- Document owner: Alex Chen (eng-infra)
- Primary contact team: GPU Fleet & Capacity (eng-infra)
- Oncall escalation: GPU-oncall (pager) -> infra-platform-engineer -> Network-SRE

High-level design principles

1) Zero-trust first: every node authenticates with mTLS before joining control plane; no long-lived SSH keys.
2) Immutable provisioning: nodes are created with signed images and attested via node attestation service (NTAS).
3) Network minimalism: default-deny egress and explicit egress-shield for allowed telemetry and registry endpoints.
4) Safe promotion: CI/CD pipeline gates for terraform plan/apply, automated preflight, postflight smoke tests, and quarantine rollback.

Required services and modules

- Terraform modules (canonical names used in examples): tf_gpu_node, tf_vpc_gateway, tf_egress_shield, tf_kms_integration, tf_warm_pool_registration.
- Runtime services: gpu-allocator, warm-pool-registry, kv-cache-rebuilder (runtime team).
- Network components: egress-shield-proxy (HTTP+TLS), nat-gateway with egress quotas, private endpoint for control-plane API.

Preflight checklist (automated and manual)

1) IaC lint and static checks (automated)
   - terraform fmt && terraform validate
   - tflint with our policy plugin (checks module inputs, IAM least-privilege)
2) Image provenance (automated)
   - Verify image signature against KMS/HSM: cosign verify --key kms://alias/redwood-edge <image>
3) Networking & DNS (automated)
   - Validate route table entries, private link endpoints, and that egress-shield is addressable from the new subnet.
4) Identity & attestation (manual automated)
   - Confirm NTAS policy exists for new site id (site-zone tag).
5) Capacity & thermal (manual)
   - Confirm on-site power/PDUs are in the expected list and rack-level heat budget <= 85% before onboarding.

Acceptance criteria (automated smoke tests)

- Node registers with warm-pool registry within 300s after bootstrap.
- Control-plane health check: /healthz returns 200 over mTLS (mutual TLS) using node cert.
- Tokenized egress: requests to package registry succeed via egress-shield proxy; all other egress flows are blocked.
- Warm-pool metrics: available_warm_nodes >= 2 for the first 10 minutes.

Terraform example (pattern)

```
module "gpu_node" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-infra/tf_gpu_node?ref=v1.4.0"
  site_id = var.site_id
  node_count = var.node_count
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  image_signed_digest = var.image_signed_digest
  kms_key = module.kms.edge_signing_key_id
  subnet_id = module.vpc.edge_subnet_id
  tags = {
    team = "gpu-fleet"
    environment = var.environment
    site = var.site_id
  }
}

module "egress_shield" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-infra/tf_egress_shield?ref=stable"
  allowed_endpoints = var.allowed_endpoints
  zone = var.region
}
```

Terraform variables table (reference)

- site_id: string – unique human-readable site code (e.g., nyc-edge-03)
- node_count: number – initial nodes to provision (start small, 1–8)
- instance_type: string – instance or board SKU (gpu.a100-40gb)
- image_signed_digest: string – cosign digest for signed image
- allowed_endpoints: list of strings – egress targets for shield (registry, metrics, ntas)

CI/CD pipeline (Buildkite example)

- Branching model: feature branch -> infra review -> merge to staging -> integration tests -> promote to production.
- Two-stage apply: staging apply (non-production site tag) then production apply gated by owner approval and preflight green.

Example job snippet:

```
steps:
  - label: "terraform: plan"
    command: "./scripts/ci/terraform-plan.sh $BUILDKITE_BRANCH"
    agents: { queue: "infra-ci" }
  - wait
  - block: "Approve staging apply"
  - label: "terraform: apply staging"
    command: "./scripts/ci/terraform-apply.sh staging"
  - label: "smoke: onboarding checks"
    command: "./scripts/ci/onboard-smoke.sh"
    retry: 2
  - block: "Approve production apply"
  - label: "terraform: apply prod"
    command: "./scripts/ci/terraform-apply.sh prod"
```

Promotion safety gates

1) PR must have owner_team and at least two reviewers from GPU fleet and Network-SRE.
2) tflint policy violations block merge.
3) Auto-created plan is posted to the PR with cost delta estimate. Any delta > $1,000/mo must have finance review.
4) Staging apply must pass smoke tests and sit for 30 minutes to allow telemetry sampling.

Runbook: day-0 onboarding (fast path)

1) Author PR with module inputs and signed image digest. Include runbook checklist in PR description.
2) CI runs plan -> address feedback -> merge to staging.
3) Approve staging apply (oncall or owner) -> terraform apply staging.
4) Wait for node bootstrap (watch warm-pool-registry).
5) Run smoke script: ./scripts/ci/onboard-smoke.sh --site $site_id.
6) If smoke passes, wait 30 minutes and review telemetry (cpu/thermal/egress errors).
7) Approve production apply -> terraform apply prod.

Rollback and quarantine

- If nodes fail to register or repeatedly crash within first 20 minutes, run: terraform destroy -target=module.gpu_node 
- Quarantine network: apply egress-shield rule that blackholes non-control-plane traffic for the site until remediation.
- For image failures, revert to last signed digest and trigger a redeploy.

Operational alerts and SLOs

- Alert: Node registration failure spike (>3 nodes failing in 15m) -> page GPU-oncall.
- Alert: Warm-pool undersupply (available_warm_nodes < 2) -> page GPU-oncall and scale policy.
- SLO: first-node-registration <= 300s (p95) after successful terraform apply.
- SLO: no unapproved egress flows observed in the first 30 minutes.

Testing matrix (minimum)

- Unit: tflint + terraform validate + module unit tests (mocks).
- Integration: apply to staging virtual site with synthetic registry and telemetry endpoints.
- Chaos: simulate egress failure and preemption in staging to validate fallback and warm-pool resilience.

Operational notes and tips

- Prefer small batches for first rollout (1–3 nodes) when onboarding new sites.
- Use cosign image digests to avoid drift and accidental image updates during rollout.
- Keep egress whitelist tight; any new registry must be added via PR and pass security review.
- Annotate PRs with capacity-impact: low|medium|high for finance visibility.

Related documents

- See egress-shielding playbook for implementation details and firewall rules.
- See warm-pool registration API spec for registration protocol and guaranteed response codes.

Appendix: quick commands

- Local plan: TF_LOG=info terraform plan -var="site_id=nyc-edge-03"
- Validate image signature: cosign verify --key kms://alias/redwood-edge ghcr.io/redwood/edge-image@sha256:deadbeef
- Run smoke locally: ./scripts/ci/onboard-smoke.sh --site nyc-edge-03

End of document
